short: A traditional song also called The Yellow Handkerchief.
note: Flash Company is a traditional song about love, dissipation, and lost prosperity, also known as The Yellow Handkerchief. It is catalogued as Roud 954.

sources.label: The Traditional Ballad Index: The Yellow Handkerchief

short: A hinged traveling bag named after W. E. Gladstone.
note: A Gladstone bag is a small suitcase that opens into two equal compartments. It was named for the British statesman William Ewart Gladstone.

short: The sailor’s name in a traditional disguised-woman ballad.
note: Jack Monroe, also called Jack-A-Roe and Jack the Sailor, is a traditional ballad in which a woman goes to sea in male disguise to find her lover. Its variants circulated in Britain and North America.

sources.label: Smithsonian Folkways: Edna Ritchie, ballad liner notes

short: A stringed instrument played by the wind.
note: An aeolian harp sounds when moving air excites its stretched strings. The name refers to Aeolus, the keeper or ruler of winds in Greek mythology.

sources.label: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Aeolian Harp

short: The spar carrying a sail above the topsail.
note: A yard is a horizontal spar supporting a square sail. The topgallant is the mast or sail section above the topmast and topsail.

short: A forward-running support for a ship’s foremast.
note: A fixed rope or cable running from the foremast toward the bow, supporting the mast from the front.

short: The pulley housings in rope tackle.
note: A block holds one or more pulley wheels through which a rope passes. Connected blocks and rope make tackle for lifting or hauling.

short: Stephen Foster’s well-known song, published in 1848.
note: Stephen Foster’s Oh! Susanna is an American popular song first published in 1848. Its refrain follows a banjo-playing traveler setting out from Alabama.

short: Musical studies for practicing a particular technique.
note: From French étude, study. An étude is a composition designed to develop instrumental skill; many are also performed as concert pieces.

short: The goat-footed Greek god of shepherds and wild places.
note: Pan is a rustic Greek god associated with flocks, shepherds, mountains, and woodland. He is traditionally shown with goat’s horns and legs and plays a set of reed pipes.

short: Possibly Iscah, a biblical name connected with seeing.
note: Possibly a form of Iscah, named in Genesis 11:29 as Haran’s daughter. Traditional explanations connect the name with a root meaning to see or watch; the precise etymology is uncertain.

short: A 74-gun warship of Admiral Nelson’s era.
note: A seventy-four was a sailing ship of the line mounting 74 guns. Horatio Nelson (1758–1805), the British admiral, commanded the 74-gun Vanguard at the Battle of the Nile in 1798.

sources.label: Royal Museums Greenwich: The Battle of the Nile, 1798
